speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry can provide an update on tripartite discussions on advance Mandatory Retrenchment Notification (MRN); and (b) how does Singapore’s MRN framework compare with international peers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Not all jurisdictions require employers to notify their governments when conducting retrenchments.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And among those countries that do, practices vary.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Some countries, like Singapore, adopt a regime where notification to the Government is made within a specified period after the employees are informed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In many other countries, employers must notify the Government a fixed number of days before the employee's last working day.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Nevertheless, we have been able to achieve comparable outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: That is because employers here notify the Government shortly after informing their employees, and employees are typically informed well in advance of their last working day.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In particular, we would like to see notification to the Government happening before or by the employee's last working day as far as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Because this will enable timely employment facilitation support and outplacement services for the affected employees.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will provide an update on the tripartite discussions in due course.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I was wondering, and I think I have brought this up before on previous occasions, whether we can consider stricter penalties against those who do not comply, with this requirement.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Because as the Minister shared earlier, there are more than 20% of companies that do not comply with the MRN requirement.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: So, whether MOM will consider tougher, more stringent measures, as a form of deterrence to would-be offenders.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Currently, the penalty for non-compliance is an administrative penalty of $1,000 for the first contravention and $2,000 for subsequent contraventions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The Member would be happy to note that the majority – and I want to emphasise, the majority – of employers comply with the MRN requirement.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is an improvement from the 70% in 2024.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Late submissions were often due to administrative oversight.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Companies who submit MRNs late are issued with caution letters.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Most of these companies have been compliant thereafter.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the recalcitrant employers, we will impose administrative penalties.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Currently, the MRN compliance rate has been high.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We do not see a need to raise the penalties at this point in time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I want to emphasise, at this point in time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Nevertheless, we will review our enforcement approach and our penalties regularly.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And we will work closely with our tripartite partners, and we will assess if there is a need to review and to raise the penalties.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: I understand the intent behind the early notification, to better support displaced workers.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Based on past data, most workers take a few months to secure the next job.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: In that context, may I ask whether there is evidence that advancing notification by a short period materially improves re-employment outcomes beyond providing just earlier visibility?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, many employers have actually shared that restructuring decisions are often iterative and only finalised when all options to preserve jobs have been exhausted.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Given these trade-offs, could the Minister elaborate on whether tripartite discussions are considering an alternative approach, one that focuses less on mandating earlier notification, but more on strengthening immediate post-notification support, such as rapid job matching, industry redeployment and place-and-train mechanism, which I believe may have more direct impact on worker outcomes?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But we can go back, assess and check, and trawl through our available data to see whether we have such data.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will continue with our efforts to support all retrenched locals.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To the Member's second point, we recognise that if we require all companies to notify the Government in advance, in some cases, that requirement could inadvertently affect our workers adversely; not to the same desired impact that we want to to help our workers with.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: From many accounts, many discussions that we have had with employers, during retrenchments, which is often a painful process, many companies do try to preserve as many jobs as possible through backend negotiations.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we are conscious and we are mindful of that potential impact if we want to mandate advance notification.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our tripartite partners are indeed mindful of such concerns and they will continue to take a very careful and balanced approach in the discussions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Such discussions are still ongoing because of the review of the Employment Act.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that gives you the reassurance that this series of discussions, even as we are now debating it, answering this Parliamentary Question in the House, at the backend, these negotiations and discussions are ongoing.
